prompt_text: I need braces or Invisalign in Denver. Which specific orthodontists should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best orthodontist in Denver for braces or Invisalign?
answer_verbatim:
I can do that — but before I give specific names it would help to know a couple quick things:
- Where in Denver do you want treatment (zip code or neighborhood)?  
- Is this for you or a child/teen?  
- Do you have dental insurance that covers orthodontics, or a budget range?  
- Do you already prefer braces vs Invisalign, or are you undecided?

If you want me to look up and list current local practices I can do that once you give your neighborhood/zip code. I can’t browse the web in real time from this chat, so if you want an immediately up-to-date list you can either give a location and I’ll provide a short set of likely top options plus exactly what to ask when you call, or you can run a quick search using the links below I’ll point you to.

Meanwhile, here’s a practical plan so your first calls get the information you need — and how to pick which orthodontists to actually visit:

How to pick which orthodontists to call
- Prioritize board-certified orthodontists (DDS/DMD plus a 2–3 year orthodontic residency). Verify membership in the American Association of Orthodontists (AAO).  
- If you want Invisalign, ask whether the orthodontist is an Invisalign provider and what level (e.g., Premier/Gold/Platinum/Diamond). Higher-level providers typically have treated more cases but even newer providers can be excellent.  
- Look for experience with your case type (adult treatment, surgical cases, crowding, relapsed cases).  
- Read recent patient reviews (Google, Yelp) and look at before/after photos on the practice website or Instagram.  
- Consider logistics: office location, available hours, financing plans, insurance participation, and emergency care policies.  
- Check whether they use digital scans (iTero or similar), 3D imaging (CBCT) when needed, and offer modern options (clear ceramic braces, lingual braces, accelerated orthodontics) if these matter to you.

Questions to ask on the phone (short script)
- “Do you treat adults/children? Do you see Invisalign cases?”  
- “Do you have a current AAO board-certified orthodontist on staff?”  
- “Are you an Invisalign provider? If yes, about how many Invisalign cases have you treated?”  
- “Do you offer a complimentary or low-cost consultation and digital scan/X-rays? What is the consultation fee?”  
- “Rough estimate: typical treatment length/cost for adult Invisalign vs braces for moderate crowding?”  
- “Do you accept my insurance (name your insurer) and what financing options do you offer?”  
- “What is your emergency policy if a bracket/wire breaks?”

What to expect at an initial consult
- Discussion of goals, clinical exam, possibly photos, digital scans or X-rays.  
- Treatment options explained (braces vs Invisalign vs other).  
- A written estimate with treatment length, appliance type, cost, and payment/insurance details.  
- Opportunity to meet staff and see before/after cases.

Places to consider calling in Denver (how to find them)
- Use the Invisalign Provider Locator on Invisalign.com and filter by Denver — it lists practices and their provider level.  
- Use AAO’s “Find an Orthodontist” at aaoinfo.org and search Denver.  
- Search Google Maps for “orthodontist near [your neighborhood]” and prioritize practices with many recent reviews and before/after photos.  
- Consider the University of Colorado School of Dental Medicine orthodontic clinic (Anschutz) if cost is a concern — teaching clinics can be lower-cost and are supervised by faculty.

If you’d like, tell me your zip code/neighborhood and whether this is for an adult or child and I will:
- Give a short list (3–6) of specific Denver-area orthodontic practices to call, with reasons for each (Invisalign experience, board certification, location, hours, specialties).  
- Provide a personalized script and a recommended order of whom to call first based on your priorities (cost, speed, invisibility of the appliance, surgical expertise, etc.).
